newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS-Vereinsbank buys into consumer credit niche.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Vereinsbank buys into consumer credit niche.

text.p: Germany's Bayerische Vereinsbank AG said on Wednesday it planned to buy consumer credit specialist Noris Verbraucherbank GmbH in a move that would boost its position in the niche and add 280,000 new clients.

The bank is to merge Noris with its own consumer credit unit Franken WKV Bank AG to create a unit with deposits of 4.5 billion marks ($2.6 billion) -- giving it a share in the consumer credit market of more than two percent, according to analysts.

The new unit will have a network of more than 100 branches across Germany, 370,000 customers, a lending volume of 3.6 billion marks, and bring cost savings of some 130 million marks, Vereinsbank officials told a news conference.
"The (merged) bank will be in a position to significantly expand its market position through this acquired earnings power," Vereinsbank said in a statement.
"With the purchase of Noris Verbraucherbank, Vereinsbank ... is obtaining a well established brand in consumer banking and a branch network which ideally complements Franken WKV."
Analysts played down the significance of the move, noting that Noris represented only a tiny part of Vereinsbank's business. Vereinsbank's lending volume in 1996 was 312.3 billion marks.
The price of the takeover was not disclosed, but is estimated by analysts at some 170 million marks, on the basis of a one-to-one price to book ratio.
Schickedanz, Noris's previous owner, has withdrawn from branch-based banking and will concentrate on telephone banking through its subsidiary Quelle-Bank, Vereinsbank said.
"It remains to be seen what this will mean for Vereinsbank," said Christine Winkler, bank analyst at fellow-Bavarian bank Bayerische Hypotheken und Wechsel-Bank AG.
"Vereinsbank had not been making any money from WKV and I suppose they thought, why not?" she added.
However Winkler warned that consumer credit -- which provides no-frills, fast loans to clients wanting minimal red tape -- was high risk as well as being high-margin.

The Bavarian mortgage specialist says it aims for a 30 percent return on equity from the merged bank unit, as job cuts and other synergy effects improve profitability. WKV has 20 percent return on equity at present.
The synergies will result from the harmonisation of product ranges and the transfer of data processing systems from WKV to Noris, Vereinsbank said.
Wednesday's announcement did not come as a complete surprise. Noris said last week it was seeking a partner and there had been speculation that Vereinsbank may be a possible candidate.
